w: A gravity-defying spiral staircase floats inside Oscar Niemeyer's 1970 headquarters for Brazil's Foreign Ministry, east of the National Congress. Roberto Burle Marx designed every garden around it. Named for the old Rio palace the ministry once occupied, "Itamaraty" is now shorthand for Brazilian diplomacy.
s: Niemeyer's floating spiral staircase, Foreign Ministry HQ
_facts: Designed by Oscar Niemeyer, inaugurated 21 April 1970
Gardens by Roberto Burle Marx
Located near Praca dos Tres Poderes on the Ministries Esplanade
Name is a metonym for Brazil's Ministry of Foreign Affairs

w: Brasilia had no natural waterfront, so damming the Paranoa River during construction made one: an artificial lake 80 km around, 1,000 metres up. Embassies, sports clubs and the Lago Sul and Lago Norte suburbs ring its shore, along with the president's lakeside home, Palacio da Alvorada.
s: The dammed lake that gave the new capital a shoreline
_facts: Formed by damming the Paranoa River during Brasilia's construction
80 km circumference, 1,000m altitude
Shores host embassies, University of Brasilia, Palacio da Alvorada

w: Juscelino Kubitschek, the president who willed Brasilia into being, is buried inside the mausoleum Oscar Niemeyer built for him on the Monumental Axis. Kubitschek's widow Sarah asked Niemeyer, architect of the city's landmark buildings, to design her husband's final resting place.
s: Niemeyer's mausoleum for the president who built Brasilia
_facts: Mausoleum and memorial to Juscelino Kubitschek (1902-1976), founder of Brasilia
Designed by Oscar Niemeyer on the Monumental Axis
Commissioned by Kubitschek's widow, Sarah Kubitschek
Contains Kubitschek's final resting place

w: Nicknamed Flor do Cerrado (Cerrado flower), this 182-metre broadcast tower was one of Oscar Niemeyer's final designs, opened in 2012. A restaurant sits in an observatory 80 metres up, with an art gallery in a second deck below -- both open to the public for panoramic views over the capital.
s: Niemeyer's last tower, with a restaurant 80m up
_facts: 182 metres tall; one of Oscar Niemeyer's final designs
Inaugurated 21 April 2012
Nicknamed 'Flor do Cerrado' (Cerrado flower)
Two public observatories: a restaurant and an art gallery

w: Pope John Paul II laid the foundation stone in 1991 for this Niemeyer-designed military cathedral, built tent-like in triangular section between the tracks of the Monumental Axis. Inaugurated in 1994, it serves Brazil's Military Ordinariate -- a rare Niemeyer church built for the armed forces.
s: A tent-shaped Niemeyer cathedral for Brazil's military
_facts: Designed by Oscar Niemeyer, inaugurated 12 September 1994
Triangular, tent-like architecture
Foundation stone laid by Pope John Paul II in 1991
Serves the Military Ordinariate of Brazil

w: This cluster of buildings dating to the 1970s was renamed in 1993 for Renato Russo, frontman of the band Legiao Urbana, reopening with a theatre, cinema, library and workshop shed. It has stood shut since December 2013, undone by cracked walls, exposed wiring and failing plumbing.
s: A theatre complex named for a rock icon, shut since 2013
_facts: Named for Renato Russo (1960-1996) of Legiao Urbana, renamed 1993
Includes the Galpao Theater, a cinema, library and workshop shed
Oldest building dates to the 1970s Cultural Foundation of the Federal District
Closed since 20 December 2013 due to disrepair

w: Every Brazilian president since Juscelino Kubitschek has worked from this Niemeyer-designed block, inaugurated in 1960 at the Praca dos Tres Poderes. Part of the Brasilia UNESCO World Heritage Site, "Planalto" now doubles as shorthand for Brazil's executive branch itself.
_facts: Designed by Oscar Niemeyer in 1958, inaugurated 21 April 1960
Workplace of every Brazilian president since Kubitschek
Part of the Brasilia UNESCO World Heritage Site, designated 1987
Located at Praca dos Tres Poderes

w: Built in 1957-58 on a peninsula jutting into Lake Paranoa, this was Oscar Niemeyer's design for the presidential residence, housing every Brazilian president since Kubitschek. Listed as a National Historic Heritage Site, it is used for residence and receptions -- the office is the separate Planalto.
s: Niemeyer's lakeside residence for every Brazilian president
_facts: Designed by Oscar Niemeyer, built 1957-1958
Official residence of the president of Brazil
Located on a peninsula on Lake Paranoa
Listed as a National Historic Heritage Site

w: Lucio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer laid out this plaza so the executive, legislative and judiciary could meet as equals -- the Planalto Palace, National Congress and Supreme Federal Court all face onto it. A 90kg flag has flown here continuously since 1960; in 2023 the plaza was stormed by rioters.
s: Where Brasilia's three branches of government face off
_facts: Designed by Lucio Costa and Oscar Niemeyer
Surrounded by Planalto Palace, National Congress, Supreme Federal Court
Flies a continuously-hoisted 90kg flag since 21 April 1960
Stormed by Bolsonaro supporters on 8 January 2023

w: Shaped like a truncated pyramid, this is Oscar Niemeyer's largest Brasilia building made specifically for the arts, built 1960-1966. It holds three stages -- the 60-seat Alberto Nepomuceno, 407-seat Martins Pena and 1,407-seat Villa-Lobos -- and reopened in 2024 after a decade shut for renovation.
s: A pyramid-shaped theatre holding three stages
_facts: Designed by Oscar Niemeyer, built 1960-1966
Shaped as a truncated pyramid
Three venues: Alberto Nepomuceno (60), Martins Pena (407), Villa-Lobos (1,407 seats)
Closed for renovation 2014, reopened 2024

w: The National Library and National Museum of the Republic, both by Pritzker laureate Oscar Niemeyer, opened together in 2006 along the Monumental Axis as the Complexo Cultural da Republica -- a rectangular library beside the museum's domed gallery, Brasilia's largest new Niemeyer statement in decades.
s: Niemeyer's 2006 pairing of library and museum
_facts: Formed by the National Library of Brasilia and the National Museum of the Republic
Both designed by Oscar Niemeyer
Inaugurated in 2006
Located along the Eixo Monumental

w: Engineer Joaquim Cardozo turned Oscar Niemeyer's design for Brazil's highest court into structure, completing the palace as one corner of the Praca dos Tres Poderes alongside the Planalto and Congress. IPHAN declared it a national heritage site in 2007, the year Niemeyer turned 100.
s: Niemeyer's seat for Brazil's highest constitutional court
_facts: Designed by Oscar Niemeyer, structural engineering by Joaquim Cardozo
Seat of the Supreme Federal Court (STF)
Part of Praca dos Tres Poderes
Declared a national heritage site by IPHAN in 2007
